title: Federal Reserve Reserve Balances See Incremen... | Forex News...
content: The Federal Reserve reported an increase in Reserve Balances with Federal Reserve Banks to $3.034 trillion on October 9, 2025, up from $2.980 trillion. This rise reflects a deliberate injection of liquidity into the banking system as part of the Federal Reserve's monetary policy. The increase signals the central bank's strategic efforts to manage economic stability, enhance financial resource availability, and stimulate economic activity amid shifting global conditions. Financial analysts and economists view this development as significant for credit availability, interest rate dynamics, and overall economic growth, underscoring the Federal Reserve's critical role in shaping the nation's economic trajectory.

content: According to the CME FedWatch tool, which calculates the likelihood of changes in U.S. interest rates from futures market bets, there is a rapid and unexpected shift in expectations for the Federal Reserve. The tool shows an '88%' probability of a 0.25‑percentage‑point cut in the September meeting, a '75%' probability in October, and a '70%' probability in December. These probabilities imply that U.S. rates could end 2025 in the '3.5%–3.75%' range. Analysts say the move should strengthen the dollar’s decline in Brazil and spark discussions about rate cuts in Brazil in 2025.

title: US Reserve Balances with Federal Reserve Bank... | Forex News...
content: On October 2, 2025, the Reserve Balances with Federal Reserve Banks in the United States declined from $3.000 trillion to $2.980 trillion, according to a recent update. These balances are a critical indicator of banking system liquidity and financial stability. The slight decrease, while marginal, may reflect nuanced changes in the banking system's reserve needs or Federal Reserve operational adjustments. Economists and financial analysts view this shift as potentially significant, as it could signal early signs of changes in monetary policy or shifts in banks' demand for reserves. The decline is being monitored to determine whether it represents a one-time fluctuation or the beginning of a broader trend that could influence future fiscal and monetary policy decisions.

title: Fed
content: The Federal Reserve’s balance sheet rose modestly to $6609 billion on September 18 2025, up from $6606 billion the previous month, according to the latest data. This slight increase reflects the Fed’s ongoing adjustments to balance liquidity and financial stability amid economic uncertainties. Analysts are monitoring the change closely, as it may influence future monetary policy decisions.

title: Fed corta projeções de juros para 2025, 2026 e 2027
content: The Federal Reserve’s median projections for the Fed Funds rate fell in the short‑term outlook: for 2025 the median estimate dropped from 3.9% in June to 3.6% in September; for 2026 it fell from 3.6% to 3.4%; and for 2027 it fell from 3.4% to 3.1%. The long‑term median projection remained unchanged at 3%, while the 2028 projection was set at 3.1%. On September 17, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) lowered the Fed Funds rate by 0.25 percentage point, bringing the policy range to 4%–4.25% as expected.

title: PROGNOSE/US-Fed-Leitzinsen (17.9.; 20 : 00)
content: The article presents a chronological table of the Federal Reserve’s forecasted changes to the federal funds target range. It lists the date of each forecast, the magnitude of the change (in percentage points), and the resulting target range. For example, on 17 September 2025 the Fed is expected to cut the target range by 0.25 percentage points to 4.00‑4.25%, as shown by the line '17. SEPTEMBER* PROGNOSE -0,25 4,00 bis 4,25'. Earlier forecasts include a 0.25‑point cut on 18 December 2024 to 4.25‑4.50%, a 0.25‑point cut on 7 November 2024 to 4.50‑4.75%, and a 0.50‑point cut on 18 September 2023 to 4.75‑5.00%. The table also records earlier historical forecasts, such as a 0.25‑point increase on 26 July 2023 to 5.25‑5.50% and a 0.75‑point increase on 2 November 2022 to 3.75‑4.00%. The footnotes clarify that the 17 September 2025 forecast was published on 17 September 2025 at 20:00 MESZ, that it is the second Fed decision outside a regular FOMC meeting since 2008, and that it represents an extraordinary rate cut as part of a coordinated easing of monetary policy. The source of the data is the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), as indicated by the line '- Quelle Daten: Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC)'.

title: Fed makes first rate cut of 2025 and signals more to come
content: The Federal Reserve announced its first rate cut of 2025, lowering the policy rate by a quarter point and signalling that two additional cuts are likely later in the year, which would bring the target range to 3.5%–3.75% by year‑end.  The FOMC’s dot plot shows that nearly all officials expect easing, with most forecasting three cuts, some two, and one even projecting six cuts.  The Fed also revised its economic outlook, raising its GDP growth forecast while noting a potential rise in the unemployment rate to 4.5% by year‑end and an increase in core PCE inflation, suggesting a more stagflationary environment.  These developments indicate that the Fed is prepared to lower rates more consistently even in the face of sticky inflation.
